For hydrogen-helium, it predicts the immiscibility boundary and captures droplet nucleation and growth in helium-rain simulations of a 2.2-million-atom column, far beyond atomistic modeling scale at comparable accuracy.
AI.conclusion: Trained across compositions and conditions, such learned ab initio phase-field models could serve as a mesoscopic counterpart to ab initio molecular dynamics, bridging quantum-mechanical accuracy with mesoscopic reach.

title: Nutational Spin Pumping and Dissipation
summary: At terahertz drive frequencies, magnetization dynamics enter an inertial regime beyond the scope of standard Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (LLG) theory. We reveal a nutational damping torque comprising a bulk term and an interfacial contribution that describes spin emission into adjacent metals. The interfacial term generates nutational spin pumping: a dc spin current that scales quadratically with the drive frequency. Using a scattering approach, we relate this effect to microscopic material parameters and predict pronounced enhancements in ultrathin films and low-Fermi-energy conductors. Nutational spin pumping can be detected directly via the inverse spin Hall effect or indirectly via thickness-dependent renormalization of nutational damping.

AI.tldr: At terahertz drive frequencies, magnetization dynamics become inertial and depart from standard LLG theory. The authors identify a nutational damping torque with bulk and interfacial parts, where the interfacial part drives "nutational spin pumping"—a dc spin current scaling quadratically with drive frequency—and predict its enhancement in ultrathin films and low-Fermi-energy conductors.
AI.motivation: Standard Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (LLG) theory fails to capture magnetization dynamics driven at terahertz frequencies, where an inertial regime emerges. There is a need to extend the theoretical description of damping and spin transport beyond the conventional LLG framework.
AI.method: The paper introduces a nutational damping torque composed of a bulk term and an interfacial contribution describing spin emission into adjacent metals. A scattering approach is used to connect the interfacial effect—termed nutational spin pumping—to microscopic material parameters, yielding predictions for ultrathin films and low-Fermi-energy conductors.
AI.result: Nutational spin pumping produces a dc spin current that scales quadratically with the drive frequency and is predicted to be strongly enhanced in ultrathin films and low-Fermi-energy conductors. It can be detected directly via the inverse spin Hall effect or indirectly through thickness-dependent renormalization of nutational damping.
AI.conclusion: The work extends magnetization dynamics beyond LLG theory by identifying a new interfacial nutational damping torque and the associated nutational spin pumping effect, providing experimentally accessible signatures via the inverse spin Hall effect and thickness-dependent damping renormalization.

title: Landau-like formalism for the thermal-runaway and filamentation instabilities in switching Mott devices
summary: Correlated oxides can switch to a low-resistance state when exposed to a voltage, making these insulator-to-metal transition materials promising candidates for memristor technology. Switching in materials such as VO2 occurs because of a thermal-runaway instability that leads to the abrupt formation of a hot current-carrying metallic filament within the insulator. We study, theoretically and experimentally, this bias-induced switching as a non-linear dynamics stability problem. We construct Landau free energy-like Lyapunov functions to show that both the on-state ("set") and the off-state ("reset") transitions can be described as separate saddle-node bifurcations. Starting from the reaction-diffusion equation for the heat transport, the abrupt snap-back (reset) to the insulating state is systematically formulated as a mean field Landau-like dynamics with the filament width playing the role of the order parameter. The formulation predicts an abrupt first-order phase transition with a break-off of a finite width filament across the current-controlled reset transition. The formulation is quantitatively compared against our electrical and optical microscopy experiments on VO2 thin film devices. Multi-cycle switching dynamics experiments further reveal the emergence of a stable stochastic regime following an initial electro-spatial forming phase. Beyond establishing a cross-disciplinary dynamical framework that may be readily compared to instabilities in various reaction-diffusion scenarios, the work also provides a predictive foundation for the rational design and optimization of Mott-transition-based technologies.

AI.tldr: This work recasts bias-induced insulator-to-metal switching in correlated oxides (VO2) as a nonlinear-dynamics stability problem, showing that set and reset transitions are distinct saddle-node bifurcations and that reset is a first-order phase transition in filament width, validated against experiment.
AI.motivation: Correlated oxides exhibiting insulator-to-metal transitions are promising for memristor technology, but switching arises from a thermal-runaway instability forming a hot metallic filament whose dynamics are incompletely understood. A predictive, physics-based framework is needed to rationalize and optimize Mott-transition-based devices.
AI.method: Theoretical and experimental study. Landau free-energy-like Lyapunov functions are constructed to describe on-state (set) and off-state (reset) transitions as separate saddle-node bifurcations. Starting from the reaction-diffusion equation for heat transport, the snap-back reset to the insulating state is formulated as mean-field Landau-like dynamics with filament width as order parameter. Predictions are compared quantitatively with electrical and optical microscopy experiments on VO2 thin-film devices, plus multi-cycle switching dynamics experiments.
AI.result: Both set and reset are shown to be saddle-node bifurcations; the reset transition is predicted to be an abrupt first-order phase transition with break-off of a finite-width filament across the current-controlled transition. The formulation matches electrical and optical microscopy data. Multi-cycle experiments reveal a stable stochastic regime emerging after an initial electro-spatial forming phase.
AI.conclusion: The paper establishes a cross-disciplinary dynamical framework linking correlated-oxide switching to instabilities in reaction-diffusion scenarios, and provides a predictive foundation for rational design and optimization of Mott-transition-based technologies.

title: Why polar excitons stay sharp: parity protection of the center-of-mass recoil channel in exciton-phonon scattering
summary: In polar semiconductors the Fröhlich interaction is the dominant electron--phonon coupling, yet excitonic resonances in materials such as halide perovskites remain anomalously sharp. We show that standard frozen-center-of-mass treatments of the exciton--phonon problem miss the decisive kinematic degree of freedom: restoring the exact center-of-mass (COM) recoil reveals a universally open, parameter-free $1s\to1s$ absorption channel at recoil momentum $q_*=\sqrt{2M_{\rm ex}\hbarω_{\rm LO}}/\hbar$, whose rate scales as $N_{\rm LO}(T)$. We prove that this recoil channel is controlled by destructive electron--hole interference: the recoil linewidth vanishes with the mass asymmetry as $γ_{\rm LO}^{\rm recoil}\propto\mathcal{F}_{1s,1s}(q_*)^2$, and the elastic dressing obeys the exact suppression law $S_X/S_{\rm ind}=η^2(6-η^2)/5$ within the hydrogenic Fröhlich model. The theory establishes a hierarchy of scattering regimes. In mass-asymmetric materials (GaAs, $η=-0.74$) the recoil channel is active ($γ_{\rm LO}^{\rm recoil}=2.2$~meV); in mass-symmetric materials (FAPbI$_3$, $η=0$; MAPbI$_3$, $η=-0.11$) it is killed by interference (0.00 and 0.12 meV), showing that the observed 27--40 meV perovskite linewidths cannot be accounted for by COM recoil and therefore require internal-state-changing and other inelastic channels, of which the constructive, $η$-robust $1s\to np$ resonance is the leading candidate within the present model. The Fröhlich constant $α$ alone is therefore insufficient as a figure of merit: after projection onto the correlated exciton, the controlling parameters are $η$, $q_*a_X$, and the Rydberg detuning.

AI.tldr: Restoring exact center-of-mass recoil in the exciton–Fröhlich problem reveals a universal, parameter-free 1s→1s absorption channel at q*=sqrt(2M_ex ħω_LO)/ħ whose linewidth is governed by electron–hole interference. The recoil channel is active in mass-asymmetric GaAs (2.2 meV) but killed in nearly mass-symmetric halide perovskites (0.00–0.12 meV), so COM recoil cannot explain perovskite linewidths (27–40 meV), which must arise from internal-state-changing channels such as 1s→np.
AI.motivation: Excitonic resonances in polar semiconductors such as halide perovskites remain anomalously sharp despite the Fröhlich interaction being the dominant electron–phonon coupling there. Standard frozen-center-of-mass treatments of the exciton–phonon problem omit a decisive kinematic degree of freedom, and the Fröhlich constant α alone is used as a figure of merit without projecting onto the correlated exciton.
AI.method: Restore the exact center-of-mass (COM) recoil in the exciton–Fröhlich Hamiltonian instead of freezing the COM, and analyze the resulting 1s→1s absorption channel at recoil momentum q*=sqrt(2M_ex ħω_LO)/ħ, whose rate scales as N_LO(T). Derive the recoil linewidth γ_LO^recoil ∝ F_{1s,1s}(q*)^2 and the elastic-dressing suppression law S_X/S_ind = η^2(6−η^2)/5 within the hydrogenic Fröhlich model, evaluating it for mass-asymmetry parameter η = −0.74 (GaAs), η = 0 (FAPbI3), and η = −0.11 (MAPbI3).
AI.result: The recoil channel is universally open and parameter-free, scaling with N_LO(T) and controlled by destructive electron–hole interference: γ_LO^recoil ∝ F_{1s,1s}(q*)^2 vanishes with mass asymmetry. It is active in mass-asymmetric GaAs (γ_LO^recoil = 2.2 meV) but killed by interference in mass-symmetric FAPbI3 (0.00 meV) and MAPbI3 (0.12 meV). These values are far below the observed 27–40 meV perovskite linewidths, so COM recoil cannot account for them; the constructive, η-robust 1s→np resonance emerges as the leading candidate among internal-state-changing and other inelastic channels within the model.
AI.conclusion: After projection onto the correlated exciton, the Fröhlich constant α alone is insufficient as a figure of merit. The controlling parameters are the mass-asymmetry parameter η, the product q*a_X, and the Rydberg detuning. COM recoil, though a universal open channel, is suppressed by electron–hole interference in mass-symmetric systems and thus requires internal-state-changing channels such as 1s→np to explain perovskite linewidths.

title: Gate Control Improves Routing Efficiency for Periodic Traffic
summary: Traffic movement on highways and data packet transmission across the Internet serve as prototypical examples of collective dynamical behavior in complex systems. Although enhancing traffic flow in complex networks has been extensively investigated, most existing studies focus on single-queue models. In this paper, we introduce a simple yet effective two-queue scheme with gate control that regulates vehicle entry and integrates it with the routing protocol. When vehicles arrive at a on-ramp gate, they first join a waiting queue and are permitted to enter the main flowing queue once it has emptied. This two-queue strategy is especially advantageous when highway inflow varies periodically with large fluctuations, as is commonly observed in real traffic. Moreover, it modifies the system's failure characteristics, replacing sudden, discontinuous jamming transitions with gradual, continuous ones. The approach is based on a simple rule using only local queue information, making it easy to implement and widely applicable. Beyond the specific setup studied here, it can be applied to other transportation networks under different conditions or extended to other queuing systems, such as Internet data packet routing.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a two-queue scheme with gate control that regulates vehicle entry at on-ramps and integrates it with routing, improving traffic flow under periodic, fluctuating inflow and smoothing jamming transitions.
AI.motivation: Most studies on enhancing traffic flow in complex networks focus on single-queue models, leaving the dynamics of two-queue systems with gate control underexplored despite the practical relevance of fluctuating highway inflow and Internet packet routing.
AI.method: The authors introduce a simple two-queue scheme with gate control: vehicles arriving at an on-ramp gate first join a waiting queue and are admitted into the main flowing queue only once it has emptied. This rule relies solely on local queue information and is integrated with the routing protocol.
AI.result: The two-queue strategy proves especially advantageous when highway inflow varies periodically with large fluctuations, and it changes the system's failure characteristics by replacing sudden, discontinuous jamming transitions with gradual, continuous ones.
AI.conclusion: The approach is simple, easy to implement, and broadly applicable. Beyond the studied setup, it can be extended to other transportation networks under different conditions and to other queuing systems such as Internet data packet routing.

title: Synthesis of Metal-Semiconductor Heterojunctions in Single Graphene Nanoribbons
summary: Graphene nanoribbons (GNRs) are a highly tunable class of one-dimensional (1D) quantum materials that can be fabricated through bottom-up synthesis. Precise control over GNR band gaps and band-edge alignments has established them as a promising nanoelectronics platform, but forming high-quality electronic interfaces remains challenging. Here we combine sequential on-surface synthesis and scanning tunneling microscopy (STM)-induced dehydrogenation to directly write metallic 7-iGNR segments into otherwise semiconducting H$_2$-7-iGNRs without changing the GNR width or carbon backbone connectivity. The resulting metallic segments exhibit nonzero spectral weight at the Fermi level ($E_\mathrm{F}$) and spatially extended electronic states, consistent with two dispersive bands crossing $E_\mathrm{F}$. The new metallic states are well described by an extended Su--Schrieffer--Heeger zigzag-ladder Hamiltonian. Scanning tunnelling spectroscopy (STS) and first-principles calculations show that the valence band edge of adjacent, connected semiconducting GNR segments lies close to $E_\mathrm{F}$ for the metallic segments. STS spectra recover bulk GNR properties within $\sim$1 nm on either side of the metal-semiconductor GNR interface, with no discernible depletion region. The observed GNR band edge alignment is consistent with a small energy barrier for hole injection, thus suggesting a possible route towards atomically precise, low-barrier p-type contacts for future GNR-based electronic devices.

AI.tldr: This work creates metallic 7-iGNR segments embedded in semiconducting H2-7-iGNRs via on-surface synthesis plus STM-induced dehydrogenation, without altering width or backbone. The metallic segments host dispersive bands crossing EF and form low-barrier, depletion-free metal-semiconductor interfaces ~1 nm wide, suggesting a route to atomically precise p-type contacts.
AI.motivation: GNRs are a promising nanoelectronics platform due to tunable band gaps and band-edge alignments, but forming high-quality electronic interfaces remains challenging. The paper aims to overcome this interface-formation bottleneck by achieving precise, local control of GNR electronic character.
AI.method: Sequential on-surface synthesis combined with STM-induced dehydrogenation to locally convert semiconducting H2-7-iGNRs into metallic 7-iGNR segments without changing GNR width or carbon backbone connectivity. Characterization by STM and scanning tunneling spectroscopy (STS), supported by first-principles calculations and modeling with an extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger zigzag-ladder Hamiltonian.
AI.result: The metallic segments show nonzero spectral weight at the Fermi level and spatially extended electronic states, consistent with two dispersive bands crossing EF. The metallic states are well described by an extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger zigzag-ladder Hamiltonian. The valence band edge of adjacent connected semiconducting segments lies close to EF. STS spectra recover bulk GNR properties within ~1 nm on either side of the interface, with no discernible depletion region, consistent with a small hole-injection barrier.
AI.conclusion: Local dehydrogenation enables direct writing of metallic segments into semiconducting GNRs, producing atomically precise metal-semiconductor interfaces with no depletion region and a low hole-injection barrier. This suggests a possible route toward low-barrier p-type contacts for future GNR-based electronic devices.

title: Frustration-induced multiferroicity in hauerite MnS2
summary: Pyrite-type mineral hauerite MnS$_2$ is a magnetic insulator with localized $S=\frac52$ moments. Below 48 K, it develops a collinear antiferromagnetic order, accompanied by unit-cell doubling and breaking the inversion symmetry. We demonstrate that the latter gives rise to a ferroelectric polarization of up to 360 $μ$C/m$^2$ rendering MnS$_2$ a type-II multiferroic. Microscopically, the electronic polarization originates from S$_2$ dimers that acquire a dipole moment induced by the frustrated magnetic ordering of neighboring Mn sites. We show that time-reversal symmetry leaves ferroelectric domains intact, and that domain switching necessitates overcoming a high energy barrier set by the magnetic exchange energy scale.

AI.tldr: MnS₂ is identified as a type-II multiferroic: its antiferromagnetic order below 48 K breaks inversion symmetry, producing a ferroelectric polarization up to 360 μC/m² via S₂-dimer dipoles.
AI.motivation: The paper investigates whether the inversion-symmetry-breaking antiferromagnetic ordering of pyrite-type MnS₂ can generate a ferroelectric polarization, thereby establishing it as a multiferroic with coupled magnetic and electric order.
AI.method: Theoretical/electronic-structure analysis of the microscopic mechanism: the collinear antiferromagnetic order of localized S=5/2 Mn moments frustrates neighboring Mn sites and induces a dipole moment on S₂ dimers, yielding the electronic polarization; time-reversal symmetry and domain-switching energetics are also examined.
AI.result: A ferroelectric polarization of up to 360 μC/m² is obtained. Time-reversal symmetry leaves ferroelectric domains intact, while domain switching requires overcoming a high energy barrier set by the magnetic exchange energy scale.
AI.conclusion: MnS₂ is a type-II multiferroic in which the magnetically driven breaking of inversion symmetry and S₂-dimer polarization produce robust, strongly coupled ferroelectricity tied to the magnetic exchange scale.

title: Optimal sampling strategies in event-chain Monte Carlo
summary: Event-chain Monte Carlo (ECMC) has revolutionised computational sampling over recent years, providing a powerful alternative to the molecular-dynamics (MD) and Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) algorithms. Each method outperforms the ubiquitous random-walk Metropolis algorithm by advancing particles along deterministic trajectories, but ECMC achieves this without being constrained by Newtonian dynamics. Recent advances exploited this dynamical freedom to induce a collective particle dynamics that relax local density variations on fast timescales. In a foundational model of $N$ pairwise-interacting particles on the 1D torus, this led to an $O(N^{3/4})$ improvement on the industry-leading computational efficiency of MD and HMC - but with an impractically small prefactor at low/high mean particle density for general attractive/repulsive interactions. Here we present a universal framework that generalises this high-efficiency sampling strategy to all translationally symmetric pairwise models on the torus - creating the potential to surpass MD and HMC as the state of the art. We also numerically elucidate the collective particle dynamics and discuss broad impact across the physical sciences and computational statistics.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a universal framework generalizing a high-efficiency Event-chain Monte Carlo (ECMC) sampling strategy to all translationally symmetric pairwise models on the 1D torus, potentially surpassing MD and HMC as the state of the art.
AI.motivation: ECMC has emerged as a powerful alternative to molecular dynamics (MD) and Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC), outperforming the random-walk Metropolis algorithm by advancing particles along deterministic trajectories without Newtonian-dynamics constraints. A prior advance used this dynamical freedom to induce collective particle dynamics, achieving an O(N^{3/4}) efficiency improvement over MD and HMC in a foundational 1D torus model—but with an impractically small prefactor at low/high mean particle density for general attractive/repulsive interactions.
AI.method: The authors develop a universal framework that generalizes the high-efficiency sampling strategy to all translationally symmetric pairwise models on the torus.
AI.result: The framework extends the high-efficiency strategy beyond the foundational model, creating the potential to surpass MD and HMC as the state of the art. The collective particle dynamics are also numerically elucidated.
AI.conclusion: The work establishes a universal ECMC framework with broad impact across the physical sciences and computational statistics.

title: Phonon interference induced by defect pairs
summary: The coherent dynamics of lattice waves is of significant importance for exploring the nonadiabatic phenomena of the electron-phonon coupling under nonequilibrium conditions. Here, we propose a theoretical model for phonon interference induced by a defect pair, in which lattice waves with the selective modes are launched independently by each of defects due to the strongly local electron-phonon coupling. We find that the intensities of phonon interference fringes could be directly evaluated by a measurable quantity in experiments--Huang-Rhys factor, and the geometry of interference patterns could be modified by the internal parameters of defect pair, including the charge states, spatial distance, energy-level depth and localization strength. In particular, several novel quantum states, such as the Dirac-like and nodal-line topological states are emerged for the appropriate internal parameters. Furthermore, using Huang-Rhys model, we simulate the ultrafast optical spectroscopy in the phonon interference duration when defect pairs are excited as the color centers, where interference fringes are perfectly matched by intensities of spectrum, similar to the $\textit{lock-key}$ pattern. These results show that defect pair, serving as the driven force for the coherent dynamical processes for multidegrees of freedom, offers an ideal platform to explore fundamental quantum phenomena in nonequilibrium and ultrafast physics.

AI.tldr: A theoretical model shows that phonon interference induced by a defect pair can be tuned by defect parameters, yielding topological states, and can be read out via the Huang-Rhys factor and ultrafast optical spectra.
AI.motivation: Coherent lattice-wave dynamics is key to understanding nonadiabatic electron-phonon coupling far from equilibrium, yet a controllable platform to study such coherent phonon phenomena is lacking.
AI.method: The authors build a theoretical model of phonon interference generated by a defect pair, where each defect independently launches selective lattice-wave modes via strong local electron-phonon coupling. They evaluate fringe intensities through the Huang-Rhys factor and simulate ultrafast optical spectroscopy using the Huang-Rhys model when the defect pairs act as color centers.
AI.result: Interference-fringe intensities are directly quantified by the measurable Huang-Rhys factor. Interference-pattern geometry is tunable by defect-pair internal parameters (charge state, spatial distance, energy-level depth, localization strength). Novel quantum states, including Dirac-like and nodal-line topological states, emerge at appropriate parameters. Simulated ultrafast spectra reproduce the interference fringes in a lock-key matching pattern.
AI.conclusion: Defect pairs act as a driven force for coherent multi-degree-of-freedom dynamics and provide an ideal platform for exploring fundamental quantum phenomena in nonequilibrium and ultrafast physics.

title: Additive solid immersion lenses for enhanced collection efficiency of shallow NV centers by pulsed laser deposition and structurization of high-k amorphous oxides
summary: The negatively charged nitrogen-vacancy ($\mathrm{NV}^-$) defect in diamond can be used for quantum information processing via the readout of the radiative decay of the excited state into the ground state. The large refractive index mismatch of diamond and air causes low photon extraction efficiency due to total internal reflection losses. Here, we investigate the photon extraction numerically and report additive solid immersion lenses (SILs) consisting of the high-k dielectric yttria-stabilized-zirconia (YSZ) for surface modification and enhanced light extraction of shallow implanted nitrogen-vacancy centers. We demonstrate an average increase of 63% in saturation intensity using a scalable bottum up room temperature pulsed laser deposition and photolithography structurization process. The average necessary laser intensity for saturation is reduced by 33% by the SILs.

AI.tldr: Additive yttria-stabilized-zirconia solid immersion lenses are fabricated on diamond via pulsed laser deposition and photolithography to enhance photon extraction from shallow NV centers, yielding a 63% average increase in saturation intensity and a 33% reduction in the required saturation laser intensity.
AI.motivation: The negatively charged nitrogen-vacancy center in diamond is a promising platform for quantum information processing through readout of radiative decay from the excited to the ground state. However, the large refractive index mismatch between diamond and air causes total internal reflection losses and consequently low photon extraction efficiency.
AI.method: The authors numerically investigate photon extraction and fabricate additive solid immersion lenses made of the high-k dielectric yttria-stabilized-zirconia (YSZ) for surface modification and enhanced light extraction from shallow implanted NV centers. The structuring employs a scalable bottom-up, room-temperature pulsed laser deposition and photolithography process.
AI.result: An average increase of 63% in saturation intensity is demonstrated, and the average laser intensity necessary for saturation is reduced by 33% by the solid immersion lenses.
AI.conclusion: Additive YSZ solid immersion lenses fabricated by a scalable room-temperature process effectively enhance light extraction from shallow NV centers in diamond, improving saturation behavior and reducing the required excitation intensity.

title: Magnetic Phase Diagrams and Spin Hamiltonian of Monoclinic $α$-RuCl$_3$ from Angle-Dependent Torque Studies
summary: The layered honeycomb $α$-RuCl$_3$ has been much explored as a candidate to display unconventional cooperative magnetism between spin-orbit entangled $j_{\rm eff}=1/2$ Ru$^{3+}$ magnetic moments stabilized by strongly-frustrated, Kitaev and other bond-dependent anisotropic interactions. Most studies so far have focused on relatively large single crystals that undergo a structural phase transition from monoclinic to rhombohedral upon cooling below 150 K and a magnetic transition to zigzag order around 7 K. Here we study the magnetism of high-quality, very small (sub 100 $μ$m diameter) single crystals, which remain monoclinic upon cooling to low temperatures and display a sharp magnetic transition at 14 K. Using highly-sensitive piezo-cantilever magnetic torque measurements in fields up to 16 T, we report a comprehensive study of the magnetic phase diagrams for magnetic field rotated in three orthogonal crystallographic planes. Our extensive torque data collected upon varying almost continuously the angular orientation of the field as well as the field magnitude, allows clear detection of phase transitions via anomalies in the raw torque data and its higher order derivatives with respect to both angle and field magnitude. The obtained magnetic phase diagrams show many differences compared to rhombohedral samples, displaying reduced rotational symmetry, substantially higher fields required to suppress the spontaneous magnetic order, and distinct field-induced phases. We provide a direct comparison of the torque data with mean-field calculations for magnetic Hamiltonians appropriate for $α$-RuCl$_3$ allowing for the monoclinic lattice symmetry and propose minimal magnetic structure models for all explored regions of the magnetic phase diagrams.

AI.tldr: Magnetic torque measurements on small monoclinic α-RuCl₃ single crystals reveal distinct magnetic phase diagrams with reduced rotational symmetry, higher suppression fields, and new field-induced phases compared to rhombohedral samples.
AI.motivation: α-RuCl₃ is a leading candidate for Kitaev physics with spin-orbit entangled jeff=1/2 moments, but prior studies focused on large crystals that transition to rhombohedral symmetry on cooling. The authors target sub-100 μm crystals that remain monoclinic, to probe how lattice symmetry affects the magnetic Hamiltonian and phase behavior.
AI.method: Highly sensitive piezo-cantilever magnetic torque measurements up to 16 T on high-quality small single crystals, with field rotated in three orthogonal crystallographic planes. Phase transitions identified via anomalies in raw torque and its higher-order derivatives with respect to angle and field magnitude. Data compared with mean-field calculations of magnetic Hamiltonians incorporating monoclinic symmetry.
AI.result: Small crystals remain monoclinic at low temperature and show a sharp magnetic transition at 14 K instead of ~7 K. The magnetic phase diagrams differ substantially from rhombohedral samples: reduced rotational symmetry, much higher fields needed to suppress spontaneous order, and distinct field-induced phases. Minimal magnetic structure models are proposed for all explored regions.
AI.conclusion: Lattice symmetry strongly governs the magnetism of α-RuCl₃; monoclinic samples exhibit qualitatively different phase diagrams, and the torque data can be rationalized by mean-field Hamiltonians that explicitly account for monoclinic symmetry.

title: Scalar field theory for (chiral) active Brownian particles: bottom-up derivation revisited
summary: The active Brownian particle (ABP) model is one of the most widely used particle-based models in studies of scalar active fluids. A collection of interacting ABPs is known to exhibit intriguing phenomena that are absent in equilibrium counterparts. A prominent example is spontaneous phase separation, known as motility-induced phase separation (MIPS), which occurs even in the absence of explicit attractive interactions. In parallel, the large-scale behavior of scalar active fluids is often modeled using continuum descriptions, namely, scalar field theories. Such scalar active field theories are usually formulated in a top-down manner, and establishing their connections to particle-based models remains challenging, with these connections not yet fully understood. To advance the microscopic derivation of scalar active field theories, we revisit the connection between ABPs interacting via a two-body potential in two dimensions and scalar field theories that include all possible terms up to fourth order in spatial gradients. Our approach is based on a pressure expansion and the renormalization group (RG) method in the context of singular perturbation theory. The RG method provides a systematic way to eliminate fast variables and identify the dynamics on the slow invariant manifold. Within this framework, scalar field theories can be obtained as RG flow equations. We also apply this method to a chiral variant of the ABP model, the chiral ABP (cABP) model, in which a constant torque biases particle rotation to the left or right. We show that the scalar field theory corresponding to the cABP model contains two ``odd'' terms in addition to those present in the scalar field theory for ABPs. The method developed here may also be useful for deriving hydrodynamic descriptions of other types of active matter systems.

AI.tldr: This paper microscopically derives scalar active field theories from particle-based active Brownian particle (ABP) models using a pressure expansion combined with the renormalization group (RG) method in singular perturbation theory, and extends the approach to chiral ABPs.
AI.motivation: Scalar active field theories are typically formulated top-down, and their connection to underlying particle-based models such as ABPs remains challenging and not fully understood. The authors aim to advance the microscopic derivation of these continuum descriptions.
AI.method: They revisit the connection between interacting ABPs (two-body potential, two dimensions) and scalar field theories containing all terms up to fourth order in spatial gradients. The approach uses a pressure expansion and the RG method within singular perturbation theory, which systematically eliminates fast variables and identifies slow-manifold dynamics, yielding scalar field theories as RG flow equations. The method is also applied to a chiral ABP (cABP) model with a constant torque biasing rotation.
AI.result: Scalar field theories are obtained as RG flow equations from the particle model. For the cABP model, the corresponding scalar field theory contains two additional "odd" terms beyond those present in the ABP scalar field theory.
AI.conclusion: The RG-based framework provides a systematic route to derive scalar active field theories from particle-based ABP models and may be useful for deriving hydrodynamic descriptions of other active matter systems.

title: Composite fermions in ideal Chern bands
summary: The composite-fermion framework maps the strongly correlated fractional quantum Hall state onto a weakly interacting integer quantum Hall state in a reduced effective magnetic field. We ask how this framework is modified for fractional Chern insulators, where the role of a uniform magnetic field is replaced by the nonuniform Berry curvature of a Chern band. Specifically, we construct composite-fermion wave functions for Jain states and their quasiparticles and quasiholes in Aharonov-Casher bands, a widely used model for ideal Chern bands. We find that these states overlap closely with exact eigenstates over a broad range of field modulation. Using these wave functions, we demonstrate that the emergent composite-fermion band structure goes beyond the conventional picture of effective Landau levels, correctly capturing the quasiparticle dispersion. Remarkably, we find that an isolated quasiparticle band carries a total Berry flux that is different from a Landau level. These results establish a composite-fermion description for mobile fractional Chern insulator anyons and provide a framework to understand their stability.

AI.tldr: The composite-fermion mapping is extended from Landau levels to fractional Chern insulators in Aharonov-Casher bands, yielding wave functions for Jain states and their quasiparticles/quasiholes that agree well with exact diagonalization and reveal a non-Landau-level Berry flux for quasiparticle bands.
AI.motivation: The composite-fermion framework is well established for fractional quantum Hall states, where it maps strong correlations onto weakly interacting integer quantum Hall states in a reduced effective magnetic field. It is unclear how this framework is modified in fractional Chern insulators, where the uniform magnetic field is replaced by the nonuniform Berry curvature of a Chern band. Clarifying this is important for describing mobile anyons and their stability in fractional Chern insulators.
AI.method: The authors construct composite-fermion wave functions for Jain states and their quasiparticles and quasiholes in Aharonov-Casher bands, a widely used model for ideal Chern bands, and compare them with exact eigenstates across a broad range of field modulation. They then analyze the emergent composite-fermion band structure from these wave functions.
AI.result: The constructed composite-fermion states overlap closely with exact eigenstates over a broad range of field modulation. The emergent composite-fermion band structure goes beyond the conventional picture of effective Landau levels and correctly captures the quasiparticle dispersion. An isolated quasiparticle band carries a total Berry flux that differs from that of a Landau level.
AI.conclusion: A composite-fermion description is established for mobile fractional Chern insulator anyons, providing a framework to understand their stability and showing that Berry curvature reshapes the composite-fermion band structure away from the standard effective-Landau-level picture.

title: Symmetry considerations in chirality-induced spin selectivity
summary: The chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) effect, the coupling between structural chirality and electron spin polarization, has been experimentally observed across many diverse systems. However, despite extensive theoretical effort, a unified mechanistic understanding remains elusive. In this perspective, we demonstrate how some of the basic properties of the fascinating effects of CISS can be understood based on straightforward symmetry considerations commonly employed in fundamental particle physics. In particular, we show that CISS does not violate any fundamental symmetries including parity and time-reversal. By anchoring CISS within the universal language of symmetry, we offer a robust conceptual foundation for interpreting experiments and guiding future theoretical and experimental designs.

AI.tldr: This perspective argues that the chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) effect can be understood through basic symmetry considerations borrowed from particle physics, and that CISS violates no fundamental symmetries such as parity or time-reversal.
AI.motivation: CISS, the coupling between structural chirality and electron spin polarization, has been observed across many systems, yet no unified mechanistic understanding exists despite extensive theoretical work. The authors aim to resolve this impasse by grounding CISS in a universal symmetry framework.
AI.method: The authors apply straightforward symmetry arguments commonly used in fundamental particle physics—specifically analyzing parity and time-reversal symmetries—to the basic properties of CISS.
AI.result: They show that CISS does not violate any fundamental symmetries, including parity and time-reversal, and that its key properties follow naturally from ordinary symmetry reasoning.
AI.conclusion: By anchoring CISS within the universal language of symmetry, the work provides a robust conceptual foundation for interpreting existing experiments and for guiding future theoretical and experimental design.

title: Pressure induced structural transitions, coordination crossover, and optoelectronic response in divalent metavanadate CaV$_2$O$_6$
summary: High-pressure synchrotron X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, photoluminescence (PL), and UV-Vis absorption measurements were carried out on the divalent metavanadate CaV$_2$O$_6$ up to 31 GPa at room temperature. Ambient CaV$_2$O$_6$ crystallizes in a centrosymmetric pseudo-brannerite monoclinic structure ($C2/m$), where vanadium atoms reside in fivefold-coordinated VO$_5$ trigonal bipyramids. Under hydrostatic compression, the system undergoes a structural phase transition starting at $\sim$1 GPa to a lower-symmetry, non-centrosymmetric monoclinic phase ($C2$), which becomes the single stable phase above 5.2 GPa. This transition involves an increase in vanadium coordination from VO$_5$ bipyramids to edge-sharing distorted VO$_6$ octahedra. High-pressure Raman scattering corroborates the structural phase boundaries, exhibiting mode softening ($γ_3 = -0.42$, $γ_9 = -0.46$) within the mixed-phase regime (1.0 - 4.4 GPa) and sharp anomalies in mode frequencies and linewidths across 5.2 GPa. The optical measurements show complete PL quenching near 1 GPa due to non-radiative recombination pathways introduced by local polyhedral distortions, alongside a non-monotonic evolution of the indirect optical band gap. Above 20 GPa, an anomaly in polyhedral distortion and internal strain drives an isosymmetric structural modification within the $C2$ phase, marked by an alteration in bulk compressibility and stabilization of the optical gap. Comparative high-pressure band-gap measurements on the sister compound MgV$_2$O$_6$ validate the explicit coupling between cation coordination changes and optoelectronic response in divalent metavanadates.

AI.tldr: High-pressure studies on CaV$_2$O$_6$ up to 31 GPa reveal a pressure-induced VO$_5$-to-VO$_6$ coordination change with a non-centrosymmetric $C2$ phase, PL quenching, and an isosymmetric anomaly above 20 GPa.
AI.motivation: Divalent metavanadates host vanadium in fivefold coordination, and the coupling between cation coordination changes and optoelectronic response under compression is not well understood, motivating a combined structural and optical study.
AI.method: Synchrotron X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, photoluminescence, and UV-Vis absorption on CaV$_2$O$_6$ under hydrostatic pressure up to 31 GPa at room temperature, with comparative band-gap measurements on MgV$_2$O$_6$.
AI.result: A structural transition from centrosymmetric $C2/m$ to non-centrosymmetric $C2$ begins at $\sim$1 GPa, stabilizing above 5.2 GPa, with VO$_5$ bipyramids converting to edge-sharing distorted VO$_6$ octahedra. Raman shows mode softening ($γ_3=-0.42$, $γ_9=-0.46$) in the mixed-phase regime and anomalies at 5.2 GPa. PL quenches near 1 GPa with a non-monotonic indirect band gap; above 20 GPa an isosymmetric modification alters compressibility and stabilizes the optical gap. MgV$_2$O$_6$ results confirm coordination-optical coupling.
AI.conclusion: Pressure drives coordination increase and symmetry lowering in CaV$_2$O$_6$, explicitly coupling cation coordination changes to optoelectronic response in divalent metavanadates.

title: Domain-engineered ferroelectric BiFeO$_3$ thin films for efficient bias-free THz emission
summary: Ultrashort light pulses can drive transient photocurrents in solids, the basis of modern terahertz (THz) emitters. Ferroelectrics have recently emerged in this context as sources that require neither the bias voltage of photoconductive antennas nor the magnetic field of spintronic emitters, yet the ultrafast photocurrent generating the emission has remained debated. Here, we resolve this question in epitaxial BiFeO$_3$ thin films with engineered ferroelectric domain configurations, from single-domain to periodic stripe patterns. The stripe-domain film emits a THz field four times stronger than the single-domain configurations, reaching about half the output of a metallic spintronic reference emitter while remaining unsaturated at our highest excitation fluences. Resolving the emitted THz field in amplitude and phase as a function of the pump light polarization and the crystal orientation, we separate the coexisting photocurrents by their symmetry. This identifies the ultrafast screening of the ferroelectric polarization by photocarriers as the dominant emission mechanism in the in-plane-polarized films, enhanced in multidomain films by the strong built-in fields at the domain walls, while an out-of-plane polarization favors the bulk photovoltaic current. Our results establish the ferroelectric domain configuration as a design parameter setting both the strength and the microscopic origin of light-driven THz emission.

AI.tldr: By resolving the emitted THz field in amplitude and phase in engineered BiFeO3 domain configurations, the authors identify ultrafast screening of ferroelectric polarization as the dominant emission mechanism in in-plane-polarized films, while out-of-plane polarization favors the bulk photovoltaic current.
AI.motivation: Ferroelectrics have emerged as THz emitters requiring neither bias voltage nor magnetic field, but the microscopic origin of the ultrafast photocurrent driving the emission has remained debated and unresolved.
AI.method: Epitaxial BiFeO3 thin films with engineered domain configurations (single-domain to periodic stripe patterns) were studied. title: Transport theory for a generic two-arm co-propagating Majorana interferometer with Majorana fermion and edge vortex tunneling
summary: Co-propagating chiral Majorana edge modes are predicted to exist in proximity-coupled quantum anomalous Hall systems. They combine the exciting prospects of edge vortices as flying non-Abelian Ising anyons, with their fully electrical detection through anyon fusion processes. In this setup, electrical transport arises from the interference of a pair of Majorana edge states. By bosonizing the model with an additional replica sector, we generalize previous treatments to fully asymmetric configurations. We analyze a Mach-Zehnder interferometer and show that while the DC conductance does not exhibit signatures of edge-vortex interference, at low frequencies, this interference manifests as an effective capacitance. This quantity is sensitive to the non-Abelian anyon statistics of edge vortices and, in particular, carries signatures of their topological spin and nontrivial conformal dimension. We demonstrate that the thermal length $l_T = \hbar v/(πk_B T)$ is the relevant scale at low temperatures $T$, analogous to quasiparticle transport in conventional quantum Hall edge states with velocity $v$. As long as the interferometer arm lengths match within this length scale, transport signatures of the non-Abelian statistics of edge vortices remain visible.

AI.motivation: Co-propagating chiral Majorana edge modes in proximity-coupled quantum anomalous Hall systems offer both non-Abelian Ising anyons and fully electrical detection via anyon fusion. Prior treatments are limited, and the authors aim to generalize them to fully asymmetric configurations and identify a measurable transport observable sensitive to the anyons' non-Abelian statistics.
AI.method: Bosonization of the model with an additional replica sector, generalizing previous treatments to fully asymmetric configurations. Analysis of a Mach-Zehnder interferometer geometry for a pair of interfering Majorana edge states, focusing on the low-frequency response.
AI.result: DC conductance shows no signature of edge-vortex interference. At low frequencies, the interference appears as an effective capacitance that is sensitive to the non-Abelian anyon statistics, carrying signatures of topological spin and nontrivial conformal dimension. AI.conclusion: Transport signatures of the non-Abelian statistics of edge vortices remain visible provided the interferometer arm lengths match within the thermal length l_T, establishing the effective capacitance as an electrical probe of edge-vortex anyon statistics.

title: Sector-Resolved Winding Selection Rules for Structured-Light-Driven dc Currents
comment: 43 pages, 11 figures (7-page main text plus 36-page Supplemental Material)
summary: Structured light can generate electronic dc currents with azimuthal winding, yet the rules governing their winding order $m$ remain unclear. Here we identify sector-resolved winding selection rules using graphene as a clean two-dimensional platform. By decomposing the current response into local and gradient sectors at the current-operator level, we show that the winding order is determined not by the optical orbital angular momentum $\ell$ alone, but by the angular structure of the corresponding current operators together with projection onto the azimuthal direction. For scalar Laguerre-Gaussian beams, linear polarization yields $m=|\ell\pm1|$ in the local sector and $m=|\ell|,|\ell\pm2|$ in the gradient sector, whereas circular polarization with helicity $σ=\pm1$ selects $m=|\ell-σ|$ in the local sector and $m=|\ell+2σ|$ in the gradient sector. Numerical time-evolution calculations verify these rules and further show that helicity can select an $m=0$ branch, producing an azimuthally uniform circulating current whose radial profile determines the axial magnetic field $B_z(z)$. Our results provide a sector-resolved organizing principle for classifying and controlling structured-light-driven dc currents with tailored winding structures.

AI.tldr: The paper establishes sector-resolved winding selection rules that determine the azimuthal winding order m of structured-light-driven dc currents in graphene, showing m depends on current-operator angular structure and polarization rather than the optical orbital angular momentum ℓ alone.
AI.motivation: Structured light can generate electronic dc currents with azimuthal winding, but the rules governing their winding order m were previously unclear. The work aims to identify these winding selection rules.
AI.method: Using graphene as a clean two-dimensional platform, the current response is decomposed into local and gradient sectors at the current-operator level. Selection rules for scalar Laguerre-Gaussian beams are derived for linear and circular polarization, then verified with numerical time-evolution calculations.
AI.result: For scalar Laguerre-Gaussian beams with linear polarization: m=|ℓ±1| in the local sector and m=|ℓ|,|ℓ±2| in the gradient sector. For circular polarization with helicity σ=±1: m=|ℓ−σ| in the local sector and m=|ℓ+2σ| in the gradient sector. title: Complex magnetic phase diagrams in Tb$_2$IrAl$_4$Ge$_2$ and Er$_2$IrAl$_4$Ge$_2$
summary: We report the synthesis and comprehensive investigation of single-crystalline Tb$_2$IrAl$_4$Ge$_2$ and Er$_2$IrAl$_4$Ge$_2$, the first Ir-based members of the $Ln_2M$Al$_4$Ge$_2$ family. Both compounds crystallize in the tetragonal Tb$_2$NiAl$_4$Ge$_2$-type structure (space group $I4/mmm$) and exhibit easy-axis magnetic anisotropy with the crystallographic $c$ axis as the preferred magnetization direction. Tb$_2$IrAl$_4$Ge$_2$ undergoes antiferromagnetic ordering below $T_N = 25$ K and develops a sequence of field-induced metamagnetic transitions accompanied by pronounced magnetotransport anomalies, including a nonlinear Hall response. In contrast, Er$_2$IrAl$_4$Ge$_2$ exhibits three successive zero-field magnetic transitions and a substantially richer low-temperature magnetic phase diagram comprising multiple competing field-induced phases confined to relatively modest magnetic fields. The differences between the Tb- and Er-based compounds demonstrate the wide range of magnetic behavior that can be realized within the \ce{Tb2NiAl4Ge2}-type structure. More broadly, the successful realization of Ir-based $Ln_2M$Al$_4$Ge$_2$ compounds considerably expands the accessible chemical space of this family and opens a route toward the exploration of related $4d$- and $5d$-based aluminogermanides.

AI.motivation: The Ln2MAl4Ge2 family had not yet included Ir-based members; exploring Ir substitution extends the accessible chemical space and may reveal diverse magnetism and possible 4d/5d analogues.
AI.method: Single-crystal synthesis and comprehensive characterization (structural, magnetic, magnetotransport, including Hall measurements) of Tb2IrAl4Ge2 and Er2IrAl4Ge2.
AI.result: Both crystallize in the tetragonal Tb2NiAl4Ge2-type structure (I4/mmm) with easy-axis anisotropy along c. Tb2IrAl4Ge2 orders antiferromagnetically below TN = 25 K with field-induced metamagnetic transitions and pronounced magnetotransport anomalies (nonlinear Hall). AI.conclusion: The Tb and Er analogues display markedly different magnetic behaviors within the same structure type, and the successful Ir-based synthesis broadens the family's chemical space, opening routes to related 4d- and 5d-based aluminogermanides.

title: Parafermions in fractional Chern insulator-superconductor heterostructures: the role of spin polarization
summary: Most proposals for $Z_3$ parafermions in fractional quantum Hall-superconductor structures used the spin-unpolarized $ν= 2/3$ Halperin $(1,1,2)$ state. The fractional quantum anomalous Hall (FQAH) states of twisted MoTe$_2$ and rhombohedral graphene are believed to be spin- and valley-polarized Jain states, with the same topological order but a different spin structure. We analyze a trench between two polarized $ν= 2/3$ edges. Among the pairing and tunneling bilinears of the edge-mode electrons, exactly two of each have zero conformal spin. Pairing is compatible only with the neutral-mode superconductivity channel and tunneling only with neutral-mode backscattering, whereas in the unpolarized state singlet pairing and tunneling select the same channel. Since the two channels condense the same neutral anyon up to a local operator, the domain walls carry $Z_3$ parafermions, with 3 protected states per pair, whether or not the neutral channel changes between regions; fixing the fermion parity does not enlarge this count. Before the neutral gap forms, pairing is at best marginal for repulsive inter-edge coupling unless an attractive neutral coupling favors its channel; once the gap has formed, both charge terms are relevant for an inter-edge Coulomb coupling below 7/25 of the intra-edge one. The superconductor must supply even-frequency, equal-spin, intravalley pairing, which an s-wave singlet superconductor with only Ising spin-orbit coupling does not provide at leading order, whereas chiral $p+ip$ and $f+if$ states do. The $Z_3$ label is carried by a quasiparticle of the FQAH state, so no process confined to a junction whose tunneling segments are not FQAH can change it, and we expect a $6π$-periodic Josephson current with or without fixed fermion parity.

AI.conclusion: The Z3 label is carried by a quasiparticle of the FQAH state, so no process confined to a junction whose tunneling segments are not FQAH can change it, and a 6π-periodic Josephson current is expected with or without fixed fermion parity.

title: Decoding Thermal Stability: In situ Insights into Phase Controlled Phosphine-free Colloidal Bi-Te Nanosheets
summary: Bismuth telluride (Bi2Te3) is a prototypical V-VI semiconductor of interest for both thermoelectric and topological applications; however, phase-selective synthesis and thermal stability across the bismuth-telluride homologous series remain poorly understood. We report a facile and phosphine-free colloidal synthesis approach for a phase-selective synthesis of Bi2Te3, BiTe, and Bi4Te5 nanosheets with well-defined hexagonal morphology. By controlling precursor chemistry and reaction temperature, we achieved the selective formation of different phases within the (Bi2)m(Bi2Te3)n homologous series. Based on in situ heating studies, BiTe and Bi4Te5 nanosheets transform into Bi2Te3 at about 340 degree C, followed by preferential Te sublimation under vacuum or oxidation in air at higher temperatures. We discuss plausible mechanisms for these phase transformations. EDS analysis and FFT analysis of STEM images provide direct evidence for the temperature-dependent compositional and structural changes and highlight the close thermal relationship among these phases. These results not only advance fundamental understanding of phase stability and thermal behavior in bismuth-tellurides at the nanoscale but also establish a framework for understanding structural evolution in related homologous series, providing insights into their potential future applications in thermoelectric, spintronic, and topological systems.

AI.motivation: Bi2Te3 is a prototypical V-VI semiconductor relevant to thermoelectrics and topological systems, yet phase-selective synthesis and thermal stability across the bismuth-telluride homologous series are poorly understood.
AI.method: Facile, phosphine-free colloidal synthesis with control over precursor chemistry and reaction temperature to selectively form Bi2Te3, BiTe, and Bi4Te5 nanosheets with well-defined hexagonal morphology; characterization via in situ heating studies, EDS, and FFT analysis of STEM images.

title: Single-Pulse Optical Switching combined with Current-Induced Motion of Skyrmionic Spin Textures
comment: 16 pages (main) + 5 pages (supporting information). 5 figures (main) + 4 figures (supporting information). Submitted to Advanced Materials
summary: Magnetic skyrmions are promising nanoscale information carriers because their position can be manipulated by electrical currents. The additional ability of deterministic control of the spin structure would allow the use of magnetic skyrmions as multi-state bits, expanding the capabilities of skyrmion devices further. Such control could be realized by coupling all-optical helicity independent switching of magnetization (AO-HIS) to magnetic skyrmions. This is realized in a Pt/Ir/CoB/Gd/Pt multilayer that is engineered to stabilize magnetic skyrmions and, at the same time, enable AO-HIS by single ultrafast laser pulse. Laser excitation is used to write skyrmionic textures, whose polarity is selected by a small applied out-of-plane field. A single 30 fs laser pulse is then used to toggle the magnetization of an illuminated region containing skyrmionic textures, reversing their polarities without requiring any magnetic field or current pulses. This establishes deterministic optical switching of the skyrmion spin structure as a new manipulation channel, distinct from previously reported optical nucleation and annihilation. The material is then patterned into a wire, to combine the optical manipulation with current-induced skyrmion motion. These results establish a route toward opto-spintronic skyrmion devices in which light programs the internal state of a skyrmion and electrical currents control its position.

A single 30 fs laser pulse toggles the skyrmion magnetization/polarity without fields or currents, and a patterned wire combines optical state programming with current-driven skyrmion motion.

Adding such control would enable multi-state bits and expand skyrmion device functionality. Coupling AO-HIS to skyrmions is proposed as a route to achieve this.

title: Theory of Chirality-Induced Spin Selectivity in Trefoil-knot Molecules
summary: The origin of chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) remains elusive, and ultrahigh spin polarization (SP) in topologically knotted molecules is unexplained. We develop a discrete geometric spin-orbit coupling (SOC) framework for molecular junctions, resolving site-specific curvature and current-partition effects beyond continuous models. For trefoil-knot molecules, it quantifies site-resolved geometric SOC, reaching $\sim$120 meV, nearly two orders of magnitude larger than intrinsic SOC of light atoms. The substrate-coupled benzene unit, carrying the largest current and remarkable geometric SOC, dominates the CISS effect. The framework quantitatively reproduces measured SP, temperature-dependent magnetoresistance (MR) and $Δ$MR trends, establishing discrete geometric SOC as a predictive tool for CISS in topologically knotted molecules.

AI.tldr: A discrete geometric spin-orbit coupling (SOC) framework explains ultrahigh spin polarization in topologically knotted molecules via site-specific curvature and current partitioning.
AI.motivation: The origin of chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) remains elusive, and the ultrahigh spin polarization observed in topologically knotted molecules is unexplained.
AI.method: Develops a discrete geometric spin-orbit coupling (SOC) framework for molecular junctions, resolving site-specific curvature and current-partition effects beyond continuous models; applies it to trefoil-knot molecules to quantify site-resolved geometric SOC.
AI.result: Quantifies site-resolved geometric SOC reaching ~120 meV, nearly two orders of magnitude larger than intrinsic SOC of light atoms. The substrate-coupled benzene unit, carrying the largest current and remarkable geometric SOC, dominates the CISS effect. The framework quantitatively reproduces measured SP, temperature-dependent magnetoresistance (MR), and ΔMR trends.
AI.conclusion: Discrete geometric SOC is established as a predictive tool for CISS in topologically knotted molecules.

title: Flux- and tunnel-parity-controlled Josephson nonreciprocity from singlet-triplet competition in a parallel double quantum dot
summary: Nonreciprocal supercurrents in interacting nanostructures can arise when the positive and negative critical currents probe inequivalent portions of a phase-dependent many-body spectrum. We study this mechanism in a parallel double-quantum-dot Josephson junction with strong intradot Coulomb repulsion, where local and non-local Cooper-pair transfer coexist. Using exact diagonalization of a zero-bandwidth Hamiltonian with explicit superconducting orbitals, we show that orbital flux and the gauge-invariant tunnel-sign parity control the interference between local Josephson processes and non-local exchange. For detuned dots, this produces flux-tunable singlet, triplet, and doublet ground-state spectral branches and two rectification regimes. Near the boundaries of the charge sector with singly occupied dots [(1,1) sector], doublet branches compete with singlet or triplet branches, yielding diode efficiencies approaching 40%. Within the triplet-dominated (1,1) sector, nearby singlet crossings asymmetrically reshape the ground-state envelope even when both critical-current extrema lie on the triplet-like branch, producing a broader response of order 10-15%. Finite temperature generally suppresses charge-crossover rectification, however, for intermediate temperatures we find an enhancement of both the normalized efficiency and the absolute critical-current asymmetry in the triplet regime. These results establish phase-dependent many-body branch competition as a gate-, flux-, and tunnel-parity-sensitive source of Josephson nonreciprocity.

AI.tldr: The paper analyzes nonreciprocal supercurrents in a parallel double-quantum-dot Josephson junction with strong Coulomb repulsion, showing how flux, gate detuning, tunnel-sign parity, and temperature control two distinct rectification regimes rooted in many-body branch competition.
AI.motivation: Nonreciprocal supercurrents (Josephson diode effect) can emerge in interacting nanostructures when positive and negative critical currents probe inequivalent parts of a phase-dependent many-body spectrum. The authors aim to identify and characterize the mechanism of branch competition governing this nonreciprocity in a tunable, experimentally relevant double-quantum-dot geometry.
AI.method: Exact diagonalization of a zero-bandwidth Hamiltonian with explicit superconducting orbitals for a parallel double-quantum-dot Josephson junction with strong intradot Coulomb repulsion, incorporating coexisting local and non-local Cooper-pair transfer. Orbital flux and gauge-invariant tunnel-sign parity are treated as control parameters, with finite-temperature analysis of the diode efficiency and critical-current asymmetry.
AI.result: Orbital flux and tunnel-sign parity govern interference between local Josephson processes and non-local exchange. For detuned dots this yields flux-tunable singlet, triplet, and doublet ground-state spectral branches and two rectification regimes. Near the boundaries of the (1,1) charge sector, doublet branches compete with singlet or triplet branches, giving diode efficiencies approaching 40%. In the triplet-dominated (1,1) sector, nearby singlet crossings asymmetrically reshape the ground-state envelope, producing a broader ~10-15% response even when both critical-current extrema lie on the triplet-like branch. title: Structured-Light Control of Goniopolar Thermoelectricity in NaSn\texorpdfstring{$_2$}{2}As\texorpdfstring{$_2$}{2}
summary: Goniopolar metals exhibit opposite thermoelectric polarities along different crystallographic directions, enabling zero-field transverse thermoelectricity but offering few means for external control. Here we show that a spatially structured Laguerre--Gaussian vector potential can programmably reconstruct the goniopolar phase space of NaSn$_2$As$_2$. First-principles-derived Wannier transport with bond-dependent Peierls coupling reveals two OAM-dependent spatial scaling laws: the radial response follows the Laguerre--Gaussian radius $r_{\max}\propto\sqrt{|\ell|}$, while calculations for $|\ell|=2$--5 yield a dominant angular harmonic $m_{\mathrm{dom}}=2|\ell|$, encoding the optical winding in a frequency-doubled thermoelectric response. Increasing $|\ell|$ simultaneously reconstructs pre-existing goniopolar windows, enhancing a representative window by approximately 17\% at $|\ell|=5$. By contrast, reversing $\ell$ at fixed polarization produces only a small correction that approximately interchanges upon polarization reversal. Energy-resolved transport reveals that the structured field redistributes in-plane and cross-plane electronic velocities, shifting the directional Seebeck-zero boundaries that define the goniopolar state. These results establish vortex position and OAM magnitude as programmable control coordinates for goniopolar thermoelectricity.

AI.tldr: Structured Laguerre-Gaussian vector potentials programmably reconstruct the goniopolar phase space of NaSn2As2, with OAM-dependent radial and angular scaling laws that enhance and reshape transverse thermoelectric response.
AI.motivation: Goniopolar metals show opposite thermoelectric polarities along different crystallographic directions, enabling zero-field transverse thermoelectricity, but there are few means for external control. This work aims to provide external, programmable control over the goniopolar phase space.
AI.method: First-principles-derived Wannier transport with bond-dependent Peierls coupling is used to study NaSn2As2 under a spatially structured Laguerre-Gaussian vector potential. Calculations are performed for OAM modes |l|=2-5, analyzing radial scaling, angular harmonics, goniopolar window reconstruction, sign reversal of l, and energy-resolved in-plane/cross-plane velocity redistribution.
AI.result: Two OAM-dependent spatial scaling laws emerge: radial response follows r_max proportional to sqrt(|l|), and the dominant angular harmonic is m_dom = 2|l| (frequency-doubled thermoelectric response). Increasing |l| reconstructs goniopolar windows, enhancing a representative window by ~17% at |l|=5, while reversing l gives only a small correction that approximately interchanges upon polarization reversal. Energy-resolved transport shows the field redistributes in-plane and cross-plane velocities, shifting directional Seebeck-zero boundaries.
AI.conclusion: Vortex position and OAM magnitude serve as programmable control coordinates for goniopolar thermoelectricity, enabling external reconstruction of the goniopolar phase space.

title: Weak non-Landau-type contributions to the diamagnetism of graphite
summary: The exceptionally large diamagnetic susceptibility of a single-crystal graphite in the direction perpendicular to the graphene layers is caused by the Landau levels. However, there are also other contributions to the magnetic susceptibility. In particular, in metals the Pauli paramagnetism is leading, whereas in dielectrics the diamagnetic Langevin and paramagnetic Van Vleck terms are essential. These components of magnetic susceptibility are also present in graphite. In this work, we calculate the magnitudes of all these small contributions from first principles. It is found that the Pauli paramagnetism is negligible (2.3 x 10^{-9} emu/g), whereas the other diamagnetic contribution - arising from the Langevin and Van Vleck mechanisms - is comparable to the in-plane experimental diamagnetism of graphite and to the diamagnetic response of C60 and C70} fullerenes. This diamagnetic contribution proves to be slightly anisotropic (-2.93 x 10^{-7} emu/g along the x- or y-axes and -2.24 x 10^{-7} emu/g along the $z-$axis), with the averaged value -2.7 x 10^{-7} emu/g.

AI.tldr: First-principles calculations decompose graphite's magnetic susceptibility into small contributions, finding Pauli paramagnetism negligible and a substantial anisotropic Langevin/Van Vleck diamagnetism comparable to in-plane experimental diamagnetism.
AI.motivation: Graphite's exceptionally large perpendicular diamagnetic susceptibility is attributed to Landau levels, but other susceptibility contributions (Pauli paramagnetism in metals, Langevin diamagnetism and Van Vleck paramagnetism in dielectrics) also exist. Their magnitudes in graphite had not been quantified from first principles.
AI.method: First-principles calculation of all the small magnetic susceptibility contributions in single-crystal graphite: the Pauli paramagnetic term, and the diamagnetic Langevin and paramagnetic Van Vleck terms, evaluating their magnitudes and anisotropy.
AI.result: Pauli paramagnetism is negligible (2.3 x 10^-9 emu/g). The other diamagnetic contribution (Langevin plus Van Vleck) is comparable to graphite's in-plane experimental diamagnetism and to the diamagnetic response of C60 and C70 fullerenes. It is slightly anisotropic: -2.93 x 10^-7 emu/g along x or y and -2.24 x 10^-7 emu/g along z, with an average of -2.7 x 10^-7 emu/g.
AI.conclusion: Beyond the dominant Landau-level contribution, graphite hosts a sizable anisotropic Langevin/Van Vleck diamagnetism and a negligible Pauli paramagnetism, which together account for the residual magnetic response.

title: GEODE: Symmetry-Preserving Cartesian Diffusion for Crystal Generation
summary: Most known inorganic crystals exhibit symmetric atomic arrangements, yet generative models often fail to reproduce them. Explicitly enforcing these symmetries has so far yielded fewer stable and novel structures than unconstrained generation. We introduce Generative Equivariant Orbit Diffusion Engine (GEODE), to our knowledge the first model to combine coordinate and lattice diffusion in Cartesian space. GEODE first samples symmetry templates, then jointly generates the lattice, atomic coordinates and atom types while preserving the specified symmetry with a novel Wyckoff-constrained loss. Cartesian diffusion gives coordinate noise a consistent physical scale that we empirically demonstrate improves performance. Unconditional generation achieves a metastable, unique and novel (mSUN) rate of 11.9%, compared with 7.7% for the next best symmetry-aware model. We also introduce sampling time template filtering, which increases mSUN by ~6% without retraining, making GEODE competitive with leading symmetry-agnostic models. Template selection also enables joint symmetry and property guidance, which we demonstrate through classifier-free guidance of permittivity.

AI.tldr: GEODE combines coordinate and lattice diffusion in Cartesian space with symmetry-template sampling and a Wyckoff-constrained loss to generate stable, novel, symmetric inorganic crystals, reaching 11.9% mSUN versus 7.7% for the best prior symmetry-aware model.
AI.motivation: Most inorganic crystals have symmetric atomic arrangements, yet generative models struggle to reproduce these symmetries. Explicitly enforcing symmetry has previously produced fewer stable and novel structures than unconstrained generation, leaving a gap between the need for symmetry preservation and generative quality.
AI.method: GEODE is presented as the first model to combine coordinate and lattice diffusion in Cartesian space. It first samples symmetry templates, then jointly generates the lattice, atomic coordinates, and atom types while preserving the specified symmetry via a novel Wyckoff-constrained loss. Cartesian diffusion gives coordinate noise a consistent physical scale. The authors also introduce sampling time template filtering and use template selection for joint symmetry and property guidance, demonstrated through classifier-free guidance of permittivity.
AI.result: Unconditional generation achieves an mSUN (metastable, unique, and novel) rate of 11.9%, compared with 7.7% for the next best symmetry-aware model. Sampling time template filtering increases mSUN by ~6% without retraining, making GEODE competitive with leading symmetry-agnostic models.
AI.conclusion: GEODE shows that combining Cartesian coordinate-lattice diffusion with symmetry templates and a Wyckoff-constrained loss yields more stable and novel symmetric crystals than prior symmetry-aware approaches, and enables joint symmetry and property guidance, positioning it competitively against symmetry-agnostic models.
